# Advisory Review: Observed Codex Usage in JEV Drill Reports (Round 2 Focused Delta)

- **Seat**: Gemini
- **Lens**: alternative-approach
- **Review Round**: 2
- **Status**: Manual Advisory Review (Non-governed implementation gate)
- **Primary Artifact**: [`plans/detailed-usage-reporting-20261001-1610.md`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/jevdrill-codex-v0-linux/plans/detailed-usage-reporting-20261001-1610.md)
- **Delta Base/Head**: [`research/usage-review/round2/delta-binding.json`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/jevdrill-codex-v0-linux/research/usage-review/round2/delta-binding.json) (`baf70220...` -> `e77c9182...`)

---

## Executive Summary

In Round 1, this seat evaluated the implementation plan through the **alternative-approach** lens, identifying architectural tensions around stream drainage races ([AA-02]), protocol parser fail-closed behavior ([AA-03]), unobservable compaction guarantees ([AA-05]), BAML contract decoupling ([AA-01]), version probe overhead ([AA-04]), and test fixture failure semantics ([AA-06]).

The president's ruling ([`research/usage-review/round1/president/ruling-2.md`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/jevdrill-codex-v0-linux/research/usage-review/round1/president/ruling-2.md)) established five mandatory amendments (A1–A5), which have now been incorporated into [`plans/detailed-usage-reporting-20261001-1610.md`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/jevdrill-codex-v0-linux/plans/detailed-usage-reporting-20261001-1610.md) and reconciled in [`research/usage-review/reconciliation.md`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/jevdrill-codex-v0-linux/research/usage-review/reconciliation.md) and [`research/usage-review/round2/delta.diff`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/jevdrill-codex-v0-linux/research/usage-review/round2/delta.diff).

This focused delta review confirms that the revised plan fully resolves all Round 1 blockers and incorporates sound alternative designs:
1. **Permanent Invalidation & Stream Opacity (A2, closing AA-03 / RT-02 / C-1)**: Deleting "ignore presentation text" on stdout and establishing an irreversible invalid state on any non-protocol line, duplicate authoritative key, or serialization failure creates a strictly fail-closed parser. Concurrently, treating nested item payloads as opaque preserves compatibility with upstream serde-flattened duplicate keys in genuine `web_search` records.
2. **Explicit EOF vs. Error Drain Protocol (A2, closing AA-02)**: Tagged stream records distinguishing clean EOF from read/decode errors, coupled with a mandatory drain until both stream EOF sentinels are received, completely eliminates the post-exit queue drainage race.
3. **Observable Semantics & Residual Disclosure (A1, closing AA-05 / RT-01 / C-3)**: Narrowing AC1 and Behavior 4 to stream-observable conditions and structural argv exclusions—while documenting compaction, subagents, and resets as uncertified residuals in [`docs/jevdrill-integration.md`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/docs/jevdrill-integration.md) and [`docs/host-interfaces.md`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/jevdrill-codex-v0-linux/docs/host-interfaces.md)—restores testability and audit integrity.
4. **Lifecycle Failure Correction (A3, closing ADV-01)**: Classifying `timed_out` and `stalled` launches as `failed` even when process-group SIGTERM cleanup yields returncode zero closes a critical loophole where stalled executions could be recorded as `completed`.
5. **Private Adapter Opt-in (A4, closing C-2)**: Gating the probe, stream splitting, and receipt generation behind a private `codex_usage_capture: bool = False` kwarg from [`JevDrillAdapter.launch`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/src/phase_loop_runtime/jevdrill_adapter.py#L437) to [`launch_with_spec`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/src/phase_loop_runtime/launcher.py#L2098) ensures standard CLI `--json` launches remain entirely unperturbed.
6. **Designated Regression Seams (A5, closing C-4)**: Adding [`test_phase_loop_launcher.py`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/tests/test_phase_loop_launcher.py), [`test_executor_exited_without_closeout_785.py`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/tests/test_executor_exited_without_closeout_785.py), and [`test_launchspec_golden.py`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/tests/test_launchspec_golden.py) ensures modified seams in [`launch_with_spec`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/src/phase_loop_runtime/launcher.py#L2098) and [`_result_with_spec`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/src/phase_loop_runtime/launcher.py#L3880) are proven against regressions.

No remaining blockers exist. The revised plan is architecturally coherent, respects repository invariants, and is ready for implementation.

---

## Resolution of Previous Round 1 Findings

### AA-01 — Decouple `LaunchResult` carrier from JEV Drill BAML contracts
- **Status**: **RESOLVED / CLOSED** (Deferred per president ruling and reconciliation).
- **Evaluation**:
  The president ruling noted that [`LaunchResult.jevdrill_execution_run`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/src/phase_loop_runtime/launcher.py#L347) already carries a BAML-shaped host-local mapping validated by [`JevDrillAdapter.launch`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/src/phase_loop_runtime/jevdrill_adapter.py#L468-L469). Reusing this established pattern for [`LaunchResult.jevdrill_usage`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/src/phase_loop_runtime/launcher.py#L347) avoids defining a redundant intermediate type when no other consumer currently requires normalized counters. The adapter remains the single authority for validating schema conformance and reporting into the durable queue. This design is consistent with existing repository architecture.

### AA-02 — Replace premature polling break with an explicit join-and-drain protocol
- **Status**: **RESOLVED / CLOSED** (Adopted via Amendment A2).
- **Evaluation**:
  Amended Behavior 3 and `launcher.py` change boundaries now explicitly mandate:
  - Stream reader threads must push distinct tags for clean EOF versus read/decode errors.
  - Following process exit, the loop must consume queued records until *both* streams reach clean EOF under bounded shutdown; an empty queue or joined thread alone does not prove drainage.
  - Read/decode failure or an incomplete/timed-out drain permanently invalidates usage.
  This completely removes the queue drainage race condition identified in Round 1.

### AA-03 — Eliminate "ignoring presentation text" on stdout in favor of a fail-closed parser
- **Status**: **RESOLVED / CLOSED** (Adopted via Amendment A2).
- **Evaluation**:
  Behavior 4 was amended to completely excise "ignore presentation text" on stdout. In its place:
  - Every nonempty stdout line must be a valid, classifiable top-level protocol event.
  - Any non-protocol line, serialization error substitute, malformed/oversized record, or duplicate authoritative key triggers an irreversible invalidation state that later valid snapshots cannot clear.
  - Strict duplicate checking is restricted to the top-level envelope, usage, and the single `item.type` discriminator.
  - Nested item content is treated as opaque payloads, resolving the genuine upstream `web_search` duplicate `id` issue (Finding C-1).

### AA-04 — Memoize CLI version qualification to eliminate per-launch subprocess overhead
- **Status**: **RESOLVED / CLOSED** (Deferred per president ruling and reconciliation).
- **Evaluation**:
  The president ruling deferred version memoization to avoid decoupling the probe from the active child execution environment or weakening the actual CLI binding. In response, Behavior 2 was hardened to bound the probe to at most 1 second (deducted from execution deadline), isolate the probe in its own process session/group, clean up descendant processes on timeout, and bound pipe shutdown so descendant wrappers cannot hang the launch. Furthermore, the plan clarifies that [`completion_time_ms`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/src/phase_loop_runtime/jevdrill_adapter.py#L471) reflects the host-monotonic wall time of the entire launch call. This addresses the operational safety concerns raised in Round 1 without introducing cache-invalidation risks.

### AA-05 — Narrow compaction exclusion claim to observable stream semantics
- **Status**: **RESOLVED / CLOSED** (Adopted via Amendment A1).
- **Evaluation**:
  Source inspection of pinned `exec-events.rs:598` and `protocol.rs:1400` confirmed that `ContextCompacted` notifications are dropped by the 0.159.2 JSONL emitter and emit no event on stdout. The plan now explicitly recognizes this limitation:
  - Compaction absence cannot be established from stdout and is removed as an acceptance criterion gate.
  - Behavior 4 and AC1 are narrowed to stream-observable conditions and structural argv exclusions (`build_codex_command` never emits resume/fork).
  - Compaction, internal subagents, dropped notifications, retries, and mid-turn total resets are recorded as explicit residual limitations in [`docs/jevdrill-integration.md`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/docs/jevdrill-integration.md) and [`docs/host-interfaces.md`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/jevdrill-codex-v0-linux/docs/host-interfaces.md).

### AA-06 — Explicitly separate failure controls in test fixtures
- **Status**: **RESOLVED / CLOSED** (Adopted via Amendment A3 and plan clarification).
- **Evaluation**:
  The revised plan clearly separates the two failure conditions:
  1. Process failure prior to a valid terminal snapshot -> usage counters remain `unknown`.
  2. Valid terminal snapshot followed by nonzero exit, timeout, or stall -> observed counters are retained, lifecycle reports `failed`, and no completion claim is made.
  Critically, the plan preserves existing JEV learning semantics by maintaining `applied_plan_id` when the executor was available and identity matched, rejecting the overbroad Round 1 suggestion to null applied plan identity on failure.

---

## Evaluation of Additional Round 2 Plan Amendments

1. **Amendment A3 — Adapter Lifecycle Classification ([`jevdrill_adapter.py:459`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/src/phase_loop_runtime/jevdrill_adapter.py#L459))**:
   Existing code derived lifecycle solely from `result.interrupted`, `result.failed`, and `result.available`. Because [`_cleanup_process_group`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/src/phase_loop_runtime/launcher.py#L4119) sends `SIGTERM`, a child handling `SIGTERM` gracefully can return `returncode == 0` while `result.timed_out` or `result.stalled` is set. Under existing logic, such runs were incorrectly classified as `completed`. Amendment A3 explicitly maps `timed_out` and `stalled` to `failed`, regardless of zero exit codes, and mandates graceful-timeout/stall control fixtures. This is an essential correctness repair.

2. **Amendment A4 — Explicit Adapter Opt-In (`codex_usage_capture: bool = False`)**:
   Under existing code, CLI operator runs can specify `--json` independently of JEV Drill. If the launcher triggered stream splitting and usage harvesting whenever `--json` was present in `command`, general-purpose executions would incur unrequested probing and split-stream overhead. Amendment A4 passes `codex_usage_capture=True` strictly from [`JevDrillAdapter.launch`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/src/phase_loop_runtime/jevdrill_adapter.py#L437) to [`launch_with_spec`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/src/phase_loop_runtime/launcher.py#L2098). A dedicated negative control verifies that ordinary `--json` runs execute without probing, keep merged stderr, and return `jevdrill_usage=None`.

3. **Amendment A5 — Expansion of Launcher Regression Verification**:
   The verification commands and evidence reducer requirements were expanded to include [`test_phase_loop_launcher.py`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/tests/test_phase_loop_launcher.py), [`test_executor_exited_without_closeout_785.py`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/tests/test_executor_exited_without_closeout_785.py) (covering `agent-harness#785`), and [`test_launchspec_golden.py`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/tests/test_launchspec_golden.py). This guarantees that [`launch_with_spec`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/src/phase_loop_runtime/launcher.py#L2098), [`_result_with_spec`](file:///mnt/workspace/worktrees/viperjuice/agent-harness-windows-port/phase-loop-runtime/src/phase_loop_runtime/launcher.py#L3880), LaunchSpec properties, and the Codex final-message completion proofs are actively defended against regression.
